items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I figured that if Sangiorgi or Fred Palmer had been there, things would not have happened the way they did. ... the man would not pay the same price for a mixed orchestra as he had proposed to Sangiorgi when he was in Rome

ctx.x: We arrived and went to a hotel next door to the Casino. After we settled, we went to see the manager of the Casino to straighten out the hours we would have to play and any other business that had to be taken care of. The first thing the owner did was to pretend that he was surprised to see that the band was not an all Negro group and three of the personnel were Italian.

I spoke no Italian, except for a few words such as "Bon Giorno", "A-Rivederci", and "Grazie", which means 'good day', 'goodbye' and 'thankyou'. So Al Melili was interpreting what the fellow was saying. I told Al to tell this guy that it was not true that he expected the group to be all Negro because he knew that it wasn't when he came to Rome to discuss the contract. What Al told him, I don't know, but I could see that Al was afraid to speak up for our rights, and I figured that if Sangiorgi or Fred Palmer had…

I knew that Melili had not done much work since he had come back to Italy from Egypt where he had stayed quite a number of years and he did not want to lose this opportunity to work. The results of the discussion was that the man would not pay the same price for a mixed orchestra as he had proposed to Sangiorgi when he was in Rome and to my estimation, knew that the orchestra would not be all Negro.
